report:
## 1. NVIDIA Parakeet TDT (0.6b-v2 / 1.1b-v2, and v3) — the strongest Whisper alternative

- Architecture/speed: FastConformer encoder + TDT (timestamped delayed transducer) decoder, 0.6B and 1.1B English models; v3 adds 25+ European languages. Self-reported RTFx 3,386 on the HF Open ASR Leaderboard (batch 128) vs ~200-400 RTFx for whisper-large-v3, i.e. roughly an order of magnitude higher throughput; on a 4GB GTX 1650 the 0.6B model transcribes far faster than real time (typical RTF well below 0.3 at batch 1). The 0.6B model ingests audio segments up to 24 minutes in a single forward pass, which removes the chunking pain Whisper has on 2h movies. Sources: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 , https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt_ctc-1.1b , https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v1

WER: on the HF Open ASR Leaderboard, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 posts self-reported mean WER 6.05 across leaderboard sets, AMI test 11.16, GigaSpeech 9.74; the companion paper reports canary-1b-v2 beats whisper-large-v3 on English while being 10x faster. Independent 2026 writeups put parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 at 6.32% vs whisper-large-v3 7.44% on the same eval, and users report materially fewer silence-hallucination paragraphs than Whisper on natural audio. For English movie soundtracks, Parakeet is broadly at or slightly above whisper-large-v3 in WER at a fraction of the compute. Sources: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 , https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v1 , https://www.localaimaster.com/blog/parakeet-vs-whisper , https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/comments/1nf10ye/30_days_testing_parakeet_v3_vs_whisper/

Word timestamps: YES — the model card explicitly advertises accurate word-level timestamp prediction plus punctuation/capitalization. This is the single most valuable property for subtitle sync: no WhisperX-style forced-alignment stage is strictly required (though one still helps sentence grouping). Source: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2

VRAM: 0.6B is ~1.2GB fp16 weights plus activations/KV, comfortable on a 4GB card; 1.1B ~2.3-3GB fp16; int8 (CTranslate2 via sherpa-onnx) trims both well below 4GB and runs acceptably on CPU. Sources: https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/ , https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-1.1b

License: parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 is CC-BY-4.0 and the card states it is ready for commercial/non-commercial use — NOT a non-commercial trap. IMPORTANT NUANCE: NVIDIA ships a patchwork — canary-1b and several older/CTC variants are CC-BY-NC-4.0, so every model card must be checked individually before bundling into a GitHub-distributed plugin. The v2 (CC-BY-4.0) variant is the safe default. Sources: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 , https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b

## 2. NVIDIA Canary-1b / Canary-1b-v2

Multilingual ASR + AST (original 4 languages; v2: 25 European languages) with punctuation, capitalization, and built-in diarization capability; v2 derives reliable segment-level timestamps via the NeMo Forced Aligner (NFA) with an auxiliary CTC model. Leaderboard: canary-1b mean WER 6.5, LibriSpeech-clean 2.89, RTFx 235. canary-1b-v2 outperforms whisper-large-v3 on English ASR while being 10x faster and is competitive with Seamless-M4T-v2 and LLM-based ASR. VRAM ~2.3-3GB fp16 for the 1B model — fits 4GB. The deal-breaker: license is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial), which disqualifies it for an open GitHub plugin, and word-level alignment is post-hoc (NFA), less native than Parakeet TDT. Supported in sherpa-onnx. Sources: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b , https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b-v2 , https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v1

## 3. Moonshine (UsefulSensors) 250M / 500M / 1B

Purpose-built for low-latency streaming voice interfaces, not long-form media: it claims roughly 5x faster than whisper-large-v3 on a single GPU with comparable WER on clean speech, and runs great on CPU — but independent evals show accuracy on noise, music, accents and non-English audio well below whisper-large-v3-turbo. English-centric; word-level timestamp tooling is not a headline feature (streaming sherpa-onnx builds produce no per-word timestamps), so subtitle sync would still need a separate aligner. License MIT — clean for the plugin. VRAM negligible (250M runs on CPU). Verdict for 2h movies: not competitive for the subtitle-quality goal. Sources: https://huggingface.co/UsefulSensors/moonshine , https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15606 , https://github.com/usefulsensors/moonshine

## 4. Alibaba SenseVoice-Small + FunASR Paraformer

SenseVoiceSmall: 234M params, 5 languages (zh/en/ja/ko/yue), claims ~70x faster than Whisper-large (FunAudioLLM paper) and is excellent for Chinese/Japanese/Korean subtitles, though below whisper-large-v3 for general English long-form and weaker on punctuation. No native word timestamps — FunASR 1.3.29 (2026-07) restored SenseVoice VAD segment timestamps, giving subtitle-useful segment boundaries; Paraformer-zh has native timestamp output (ASR + timestamps) plus a streaming variant. FunASR benchmarks: SenseVoiceSmall 17.2x realtime, paraformer-large 15.6x, whisper-large-v3 13.4x (GPU), with benchmark WER 7.81% / 10.18% on FunASR test sets. Both permissively licensed (FunASR Apache-2.0); the community is large in the Asia-Pacific region; a CPU-friendly C++ runtime exists. Long-form stability requires pairing VAD (fsmn-vad) + punctuation models from the same suite. Sources: https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/discussions/2947 , https://modelscope.github.io/FunASR/benchmark.html , https://github.com/QwenAudio/SenseVoice , https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04051

For the 4GB card: SenseVoice + VAD is light (realtime faster than Whisper) and the natural fit for Asian-language movies; for English it does not beat Parakeet/Whisper accuracy, so treat it as a language-specific second engine in the plugin.

## 5. Qwen3-ASR (0.6B / 1.7B)

Released 2026-01-29, Apache-2.0, built on Qwen3-Omni: supports 30 languages plus 22 Chinese dialects with language identification; the 1.7B reports the best mean WER 5.76 of any open-source model on the HF Open ASR Leaderboard (RTFx 147) and is competitive with closed APIs per its technical report. Caveats for this task: it is LLM-based, so the 1.7B needs ~4-5GB+ fp16 plus KV cache (borderline/impossible at useful speed on a 4GB GTX 1650), word-level timestamps are not native (sentence-level only, via FunASR pipelines), and CPU fallback is poor. The 0.6B fits 4GB better but remains heavy vs Parakeet. A candidate for the non-English channel of a future plugin version if tooling matures. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21337 , https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B , https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR

## 6. sherpa-onnx (k2-fsa) as the deployment runtime

Covers exactly this model zoo: offline and streaming Parakeet, Canary, Moonshine, SenseVoice, Paraformer, Whisper; int8 quantization; C++/Python/C APIs; pip install sherpa-onnx; model-download scripts (fetch-parakeet, fetch-sense-voice, fetch-paraformer, fetch-moonshine). Timestamps: exposes word/segment timestamps where the model emits them (Parakeet TDT and Paraformer natively; Whisper via its built-in alignment) and has flags to enable timestamp output per ASR engine. Sentence grouping is done with VAD + punctuation + rescoring, and sherpa-onnx integrates speaker diarization too. It is the leanest way to run Parakeet on a 4GB card and the natural second backend for the plugin without heavy dependencies. Sources: https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx , https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/

## Ranked verdict for vlc-ai-subs (4GB GTX 1650, Linux, offline movie subtitles)

Nothing non-Whisper is clearly better for multilingual subtitles in the box today — Whisper large-v3-turbo + WhisperX remains the best general subtitle-quality choice (MIT, 99 languages, mature word alignment, VAD/diarization ecosystem). For English-heavy pipelines, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 (CC-BY-4.0) is the strongest non-Whisper challenger and the only realistic candidate to beat it technically: WER at or below whisper-large-v3 on English, roughly an order of magnitude less GPU time, native word-level timestamps that remove the WhisperX forced-alignment step, 24-minute segment input for long-form stability, and it floats comfortably in the 4GB card. Ranked for the plugin: 1) parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 — adopt as default English engine via sherpa-onnx, keep whisper-turbo as the non-English fallback; 2) canary-1b(-v2) — best multilingual accuracy but CC-BY-NC-4.0 blocks public distribution; 3) SenseVoiceSmall — best for zh/ja/ko/yue, pair with fsmn-vad; 4) Qwen3-ASR-0.6B — Apache-2.0 but heavy for 4GB and timestamp-weak; 5) moonshine — not for movie subtitles. License hygiene must be verified per model card: the NVIDIA family mixes CC-BY-4.0 (parakeet v2) and CC-BY-NC-4.0 (canary).
